blocks.text: Maha Japa Yagna — Community Mantra Chanting

runs.text: A yagna is sacred offering; Maha Japa Yagnas in Japam are collective chanting goals where many devotees add japa counts.
Join from the menu to participate in sankalpa with others.

blocks.text: What is a Maha Japa Yagna?

runs.text: Community targets (e.g. lakhs of japas) build shared merit and motivation. Your counts sync when signed in.

items: Play and chant — counts add to collective total

runs.text: During yagna window shown in app.
The number 108 is one full round on a japa mala. Steady repetition calms the mind and deepens attention on the mantra’s meaning.
Some traditions prescribe 11 or 21 malas — ask your guru or priest for counts suited to your vow.

items: Chanting too fast and losing focus on the sound
Mixing multiple deity vows without guidance
Expecting only material results instead of bhakti and ethical living

runs.text: Home japa supports temple worship; it does not replace darshan. Visiting the temple on festival days or Saturdays strengthens family tradition.
CTA: Menu → Maha Japa Yagnas — see live counters.

faqs.question: Same as temple fire yagna?
faqs.answer: Digital collective japa — complements, not replaces, priest-led homam.

faqs.question: Which mantra is used?
faqs.answer: Per yagna deity/theme — read details in app.

faqs.question: Free to join?
faqs.answer: Core join is free; app may show optional support (dakshina).

faqs.question: How long do yagnas run?
faqs.answer: Varies — check dates in Maha Yagnas screen.

disclaimer.text: This article is for educational and devotional practice only. Japam does not provide medical, legal, or financial advice. Results depend on personal faith and consistent practice. Mantra text and audio in the app are for japa support; consult your family priest or tradition for formal puja rules.
